title: Control Plane: annotate sensitive endpoints with RBAC v2 permissions + coverage tests
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes:
- Control Plane endpoints now declare RBAC v2 permissions for org/user/role + routing policy actions.
- Added CI guardrail to prevent shipping new sensitive endpoints without permission annotations.
- No behavior change unless RBAC v2 enforcement is enabled (feature-flagged).
body: Context: As part of RBAC v2, we need a canonical mapping from Control Plane API actions to permission strings and a mechanical way to ensure new endpoints can’t ship without being categorized. This PR adds explicit permission annotations to the most security-relevant Control Plane routes (org/user/role management and routing policy updates) and introduces unit tests that fail if a sensitive endpoint is missing a permission. This is intended to support deny-by-default enforcement in the gateway/service middleware (separate PRs), and to improve auditability by guaranteeing an action string exists for every sensitive operation. Scope: (1) Add @RequiresPermission(...) annotations for org/user/role CRUD, API key admin surfaces that live in the Control Plane, and routing policy create/update/delete + rollout/pinning operations. (2) Introduce an endpoint coverage test that enumerates registered routes and asserts that any route tagged as "sensitive" is annotated with a permission and resource scope mapping. (3) Normalize a handful of legacy endpoints to use consistent "resource" extraction (org_id/project_id/env_id) so the evaluator can be called with the correct scope. Non-goals: This PR does not enable enforcement by itself; enforcement remains behind rbac.v2.enforce_control_plane and rbac.v2.enforce_gateway. It also does not finalize role templates or migration mappings; those are handled in the policy bundle repo. Implementation notes: Permission strings follow ADR-014 conventions (e.g., org.users.create, org.roles.update, routing.policies.update, routing.rollouts.manage). Each handler now declares a permission + a resource scope extractor (OrgScope / ProjectScope / EnvScope). The coverage test relies on the router registry metadata rather than reflection on handler code, so it stays stable as we refactor handler wiring. Testing: Added unit tests for the router registry: (a) all sensitive endpoints have permissions, (b) permission strings are unique within the Control Plane module, (c) scope extractor returns non-empty IDs for endpoints that claim org/project/env scoping. Verified locally with rbac.v2.enforce_control_plane disabled (no functional changes) and enabled in a dev environment (expected 403s when calling admin endpoints with insufficient roles). Rollout: Merge is safe independent of feature flags. Once gateway/service enforcement PRs land, this ensures coverage for the core admin surface area and blocks regressions where we add a sensitive endpoint without a permission mapping. Follow-ups: (1) add remaining annotations for billing/admin and data-retention endpoints (tracked in ENG-18241), (2) wire "denial reason" detail into Control Plane error mapping (PR-28241), (3) add integration tests for key user journeys (PR-28344).
commits: control-plane/rbac: add permission annotations for org + identity handlers
control-plane/rbac: annotate routing policy + rollout endpoints (scope: project/env)
control-plane/router: plumb permission + scope metadata through registry
chore: fix legacy handlers to use standardized scope extraction helpers
docs: inline comments referencing ADR-014 naming rules
conversation: Ethan Park (review): Good direction. Two asks: (1) make sure routing rollouts are scoped to env (not project) since rollouts are env-specific in the data model; (2) the coverage test should fail on any endpoint tagged sensitive, even if it’s internal-only, otherwise we’ll forget when we flip flags in Private.

Benji Okafor (author): Updated rollouts to EnvScope (env_id extracted from /projects/{project_id}/envs/{env_id}/rollouts). Also changed the coverage test to include internal routes with sensitive=true. Added a short comment in RouteMetadata explaining why internal is included.

Jordan Lee (review): Permission names: I see org.role_bindings.* and org.roles.*. Per ADR-014 we should keep plural resource segments stable; role_bindings is OK, but can we avoid mixing underscore and dot semantics? Recommend org.roleBindings.* or org.role_bindings.* everywhere. Also we need a unique stable action string for routing policy edits: routing.policies.update is fine; rollout should be routing.rollouts.manage (or create/update/delete).

Benji Okafor (author): Normalized to org.role_bindings.* everywhere (kept underscore per existing permission registry style in PR-28134). For rollouts, split into routing.rollouts.create/update/delete to match handler granularity; kept routing.rollouts.read separate for GET endpoints. Added uniqueness assertion in the test module to catch accidental duplicates.

Marcus Lin (review): Please ensure we are not accidentally exposing permission strings to non-admin clients in error bodies. Also can we add a test for at least one endpoint to assert missing permission annotation fails registration? Guardrails are great, but we should test the guardrail.

Benji Okafor (author): Error bodies unchanged in this PR; no enforcement here. Added a negative test that constructs a RouteRegistry with a synthetic sensitive route missing permission metadata and asserts registry.validate() throws with a clear message. That should cover the guardrail behavior.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): Minor: In ScopeExtractors, return a typed error / sentinel rather than empty string for missing IDs; empty IDs can become "global" by mistake later. Even if enforcement isn’t wired, we should make failures loud.

Benji Okafor (author): Good call. Updated extractors to return Result<Scope, ScopeError> and made registry validation fail if a sensitive route’s scope extractor can’t produce an ID from the path params. Updated tests accordingly.
Ethan Park (approval): Approved. The scope fix + coverage test looks solid. Please keep follow-up for billing/data-retention endpoints tracked; those are common enterprise questionnaire items.
Jordan Lee (approval): Approved after naming normalization. Thanks for adding uniqueness and negative tests—this will prevent a lot of drift.
Marcus Lin (approval): Approved. Please link this PR in ENG-18305 and ensure we call out in the rollout runbook that annotations alone don’t mean enforcement is active.
Benji Okafor (author): Linked in ENG-18305 and added a note in the Linear ticket with the flag names.
